item.title: Angular ng-if vs ng-show: DOM Manipulation and Scope Behavior
item.description:
“Angular ng-if vs ng-show: DOM Manipulation and Scope Behavior”

When implementing conditional rendering in AngularJS applications, developers frequently encounter a choice between the ngIf and ngShow directives. While both facilitate showing or hiding elements based on an expression, their underlying mechanisms lead to significant practical divergences.

1. DOM Presence and Element Lifecycle

The primary difference lies in how each directive manages the element within the DOM structure.

ngIf: Complete Removal and Recreation

The ngIf directive instantiates or completely removes a segment of the DOM tree based on the truthiness of its associated expression.

item.title: AngularJS ng-repeat Completion Detection Strategies
item.description:
“AngularJS ng-repeat Completion Detection Strategies”

How can developers reliably trigger a function or apply post-processing logic once an AngularJS ng-repeat iteration has completely rendered all its elements into the Document Object Model (DOM)? Since ng-repeat constructs elements individually, there isn’t a direct “loop-finished” event. We need techniques leveraging scope properties or custom directives to pinpoint the final element’s creation.

Strategy 1: Utilizing Directive Scope Properties ($last)

A primary method involves creating a directive that runs on every repeated element and checks for the $last scope property. This property is true only for the final iteration of the loop.
